- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops >0.33 in 3 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–15%.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >2σ above recent 10-day mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is >10% below forecast, check sentiment history: if sentiment was neutral or bearish, model may be “too optimistic”; apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is falling, model may be “overconfident”; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
